correctness.rationale: Gaussian strict positive definiteness gives a positive denominator; the two-by-two reflection-even inverse formula follows by block reduction. Verified symbolic order-two Taylor expansions imply positive flat limits; Gaussian concentration implies positive sharply localized limits. The packaged exact-rational Taylor remainder checker verifies strict middle-shape numerator signs with wide margins; continuity ensures two distinct zeros and robust open-set persistence. No infinite conclusion rests on sampling.

value.rationale: Sign changes of unconstrained Gaussian Bayesian quadrature weights directly govern the stability constant and the ability of positive integrands to yield positive estimates. The theorem displays a robust node-design-dependent failure invisible from both conventional extreme-scale asymptotics, and it attains the sharp general half-positive bound at finite shape. The result is a structural boundary phenomenon, not a numerically optimized small accuracy gain.
